enonce_markdown: The scores (whole numbers) of a group of students in a test are grouped into classes $10$-$19$, $20$-$29$, $30$-$39$, and so on. The cumulative frequency up to and including the class $20$-$29$ is $18$. To draw a cumulative frequency graph, which point should be plotted for this class?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

For data recorded in whole numbers, the real class boundaries lie half a unit away from the class limits. A cumulative frequency is plotted against the **upper class boundary** of its class.

### Solution

The class $20$-$29$ contains the scores from $19.5$ to $29.5$, so its upper class boundary is $29.5$. The point is $(29.5,\ 18)$.

**Answer: d.** Option a uses the lower limit, option b the class midpoint $24.5$, and option c the upper class limit $29$ instead of the boundary.

enonce_markdown:
The ages, in whole years, of $50$ members of a youth club are summarised below.

| Age group | $10$ to $19$ | $20$ to $29$ | $30$ to $39$ | $40$ to $49$ | $50$ to $59$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of members | $3$ | $7$ | $15$ | $17$ | $8$ |

(a) Write down the upper class boundaries and the corresponding cumulative frequencies, needed to draw a cumulative frequency graph.

(b) At which cumulative frequencies are the lower quartile, the median and the upper quartile read on the vertical axis?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Plot each cumulative frequency (a running total) against the upper class boundary. For $n$ observations, the lower quartile, median and upper quartile are read at cumulative frequencies $\dfrac n4$, $\dfrac n2$ and $\dfrac{3n}4$.

### Solution

(a) Ages are whole years, so the boundaries are $9.5,\ 19.5,\ \dots$ and the upper boundaries are:

| Upper boundary | $19.5$ | $29.5$ | $39.5$ | $49.5$ | $59.5$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | $3$ | $10$ | $25$ | $42$ | $50$ |

(Running totals: $3$; $3+7=10$; $10+15=25$; $25+17=42$; $42+8=50$.) The curve starts at $(9.5,\ 0)$.

(b) With $n=50$: lower quartile at $\dfrac{50}{4}=12.5$, median at $\dfrac{50}{2}=25$, upper quartile at $\dfrac{3\times50}{4}=37.5$.

**Cumulative frequencies $12.5$, $25$ and $37.5$.**

enonce_markdown:
The heights of $60$ maize seedlings are summarised in the table.

| Height $h$ (cm) | $10\le h<20$ | $20\le h<30$ | $30\le h<40$ | $40\le h<50$ | $50\le h<60$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of seedlings | $4$ | $12$ | $20$ | $16$ | $8$ |

Using a cumulative frequency graph with straight-line interpolation, what is the estimated median height?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The median is read at cumulative frequency $\dfrac n2$. Find the class where this value is reached, then interpolate linearly inside that class: lower boundary $+$ class width $\times\dfrac{\text{needed}}{\text{class frequency}}$.

### Solution

Cumulative frequencies: $4,\ 16,\ 36,\ 52,\ 60$. The median is at the $\dfrac{60}{2}=30$th value, which is in the class $30\le h<40$ (the cumulative frequency passes from $16$ to $36$).

$$\text{Median}\approx30+10\times\frac{30-16}{20}=30+7=37\ \mathrm{cm}.$$

**Answer: a.** Option 40 is the upper boundary of the median class, 45 reads the three-quarter position as a height, and 60 is the total frequency.

enonce_markdown:
The times taken by $80$ workers to complete a task are summarised in the table.

| Time $t$ (minutes) | $0\le t<10$ | $10\le t<20$ | $20\le t<30$ | $30\le t<40$ | $40\le t<50$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of workers | $8$ | $22$ | $30$ | $14$ | $6$ |

Estimate the interquartile range, using straight-line interpolation on the cumulative frequency curve.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The interquartile range is $Q_3-Q_1$, where $Q_1$ is read at cumulative frequency $\dfrac n4$ and $Q_3$ at $\dfrac{3n}4$. Locate each in its class from the running totals, then interpolate.

### Solution

Cumulative frequencies: $8,\ 30,\ 60,\ 74,\ 80$.

$Q_1$ is at the $20$th value, in the class $10\le t<20$: $Q_1\approx10+10\times\dfrac{20-8}{22}\approx15.45$.

$Q_3$ is at the $60$th value, which is exactly the end of the class $20\le t<30$: $Q_3=30$.

$$\text{IQR}\approx30-15.45\approx14.5\ \text{minutes}.$$

**Answer: b.** Option 6.7 is $Q_3-$median, 45.5 is $Q_1+Q_3$, and 50 is the full range of the table.

enonce_markdown:
The marks of $100$ candidates in a test (out of $100$) give the following cumulative frequencies.

| Mark less than | $20$ | $40$ | $60$ | $80$ | $100$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | $8$ | $30$ | $70$ | $92$ | $100$ |

Estimate the lower quartile, the median, the upper quartile and the interquartile range, by straight-line interpolation (as when reading a cumulative frequency graph).
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Quartiles are read at cumulative frequencies $25$, $50$ and $75$ here. Between two plotted points $(x_1,\,c_1)$ and $(x_2,\,c_2)$, the value at cumulative frequency $c$ is $x_1+(x_2-x_1)\times\dfrac{c-c_1}{c_2-c_1}$.

### Solution

$Q_1$ (25th value) lies between $(20,\ 8)$ and $(40,\ 30)$:
$$Q_1\approx20+20\times\frac{25-8}{22}\approx35.5.$$

Median (50th value) lies between $(40,\ 30)$ and $(60,\ 70)$:
$$\text{Median}\approx40+20\times\frac{50-30}{40}=50.$$

$Q_3$ (75th value) lies between $(60,\ 70)$ and $(80,\ 92)$:
$$Q_3\approx60+20\times\frac{75-70}{22}\approx64.5.$$

$$\text{IQR}\approx64.5-35.5\approx29.1.$$

**$Q_1\approx35.5$, median $=50$, $Q_3\approx64.5$, IQR $\approx29.1$.**

enonce_markdown:
The distances, in km, travelled by $(40+x)$ delivery motorcyclists in one day are summarised below, where $x$ is a positive integer.

| Distance $d$ (km) | $0\le d<10$ | $10\le d<20$ | $20\le d<30$ | $30\le d<40$ | $40\le d<50$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of motorcyclists | $6$ | $x$ | $18$ | $12$ | $4$ |

The median distance, estimated by straight-line interpolation, is $25\ \mathrm{km}$.

(a) Find the value of $x$.

(b) Estimate the lower quartile.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The median is read at cumulative frequency $\dfrac n2$, where $n$ is the total frequency (here $n=40+x$). Locate its class, write the interpolation formula with $x$ in it, set it equal to the given median and solve.

### Solution

(a) The total is $n=40+x$, so the median is at the $\dfrac{40+x}{2}$th value. A median of $25$ lies in the class $20\le d<30$, for which the cumulative frequency before the class is $6+x$.

$$25=20+10\times\frac{\frac{40+x}{2}-(6+x)}{18}\ \Longrightarrow\ \frac{14-\frac x2}{18}=\frac12\ \Longrightarrow\ 14-\frac x2=9\ \Longrightarrow\ x=10.$$

Check: $n=50$, median at the $25$th value; cumulative frequencies $6,\ 16,\ 34,\ 46,\ 50$, so the $25$th value is in $20\le d<30$ and $20+10\times\dfrac{25-16}{18}=25$.

(b) The lower quartile is at the $\dfrac{50}{4}=12.5$th value, in the class $10\le d<20$ (cumulative frequency before it: $6$; class frequency: $10$).

$$Q_1\approx10+10\times\frac{12.5-6}{10}=16.5\ \mathrm{km}.$$

**$x=10$ and $Q_1\approx16.5\ \mathrm{km}$.**
